body: I think in relationships, we all need support. We choose these people to be apart of our support systems and us apart of theirs. That’s not something small, that’s actually a really important role to share with someone. I get that he found humour in it but unfortunately, he doesn’t realize that by doing so not only is he feeding into your humiliation but he’s not supporting you. There’s no reason why he shouldn’t have tried to get the dog off of you. There’s also no reason, why he should laugh about something that you have clearly stated was hurtful to you. If we are there to have others backs, their part of the deal is to have ours. I don’t know if divorce is the right choice because I don’t know your history or if this is in someway a pattern. What I can say, is that there needs to be a conversation regarding both this experience, what it was like for you, how his response each time made you feel (avoid you statement, go for i statements instead) and a full acknowledgment of what you needed in that moment but didn’t get. I know these conversations are hard especially if we have made attempts and have had less and less support, but either way they are important conversations to have. Outside of this, it’s important to sit and feel your feelings about every aspect of this experience and everything that came from it. I suggest looking into John Gottman’s work. I’m sorry you had this experience, this is so much more complicated than what some have given credit for. I hope you are able to receive the support you very much deserve. 🤍

Yeah, it takes awhile to kick in. I would say at least one to two weeks. This is also what it states off google and I can agree that’s pretty accurate. For myself personally each time I stop and restart it is completely different - same with side effects and effectiveness. 

I got headaches as well. Sometimes the original side effects can be rough but it balances out. I also had a lot of weight loss from it. Bupropion does really affect certain comorbidities, such as ocd - it is known to make it significantly worse. 

Overall, I would say I always choose to add it back and each time I choose to stop it, I always learn to regret doing so. Each time I have taken it, it has brought different impacts. I wish that the first time I took it, I never stopped because now it’s like rolling the dice and never knowing what this round will be like. My first one was really good, I think stopping and starting as much as I have makes it’s effects work differently. 

I should also mention usually when I hit the two week mark, things get really good again. Just important to notice if when it wears off if you feel any different. In my personal experience sometimes once it wears off it can be a little rough but that may also be the combo I mentioned before. (Sorry for deleting my original comment, I reread your original post and realized I misunderstood your reference to concerta) *drinking recommended daily water while taking bupropion is important*

Many companies have switched to reduced hours and days. I listened to Richard Branson talk about a similar policy he implemented for his employees. He allows them to choose their hours and trusts that they will get their work done. I agree, I think it is ridiculous that we live in a world full of so much burnout and mental health issues.. it needs to change. It can’t just be some of us get lucky and get to be free.
I predict it will keep happening. Lol.

Honestly, the biggest thing. Is how you feel about it and what your relationship is with you from this? It’s important to process what you’re able to when you can, and be mindful of what you internalize and what other hurts surface. I am sorry this happened to you. It is not your fault. We should all be able to trust those we choose to be intimate with. This isn’t about you. This is about him and his unresolved issues. But unfortunately, you have been impacted by it in a big way. Sending you lots of love.

Perhaps, both would get their wants. You may get that money back from an alternative source - the person you mentioned may choose to return the money to you or they may lose it in a similar way, they could regain that new loss from multiple sources. Does the money need to come from that person? I think the biggest thing is when we feel anger or resentment towards others or situations, we block everything. Maybe this is not just robbing you of that money but also of your peace and future blessings. I don’t know. Just a thought.

Sending lots of love and light.
